purpose: Held-out evaluation of the contradiction scanner. The first nine cases were written after the two original defects were fixed, in domains absent from the planted token-cost corpus. The last six were contributed by an adversarial review whose brief was to break the matcher, and four of them do: two are paraphrases it misses and two are false positives it raises. They are kept, labelled, and counted, because a corpus that only contains the shapes a detector handles measures nothing.
documents_are_ingested_together: All documents are ingested into one graph and scanned once, so a case can also be failed by a false positive raised against a document from a different case.

cases.why: Same attribute of the same subject, stated with a different predicate and a different subject phrasing. This is the paraphrase shape the fix targets, in an unrelated domain.

That verb was added to the claim extractor and is still there, so a claim IS now produced; what still fails is the pairing, because 'retention' and 'records' leave each topic with one token the other lacks. cases.why: Contributed by an adversarial review trying to break the matcher, and it does. One word differs between the two topics ('replica' against 'replicated'), so neither topic contains the other and the paraphrase route never pairs them. Topic containment is lexical; this is what that costs. One token of slack catches it, and was reverted because the same slack reports N7, N8 and N9 as contradictions.

cases.why: Also from the adversarial review, and the case that settles the argument. The second document says 'a pool of 50 connections' and drops the word 'size' the first document's subject carries. Lexically this is the SAME SHAPE as N7, where a gateway and a router are different subjects: matching tokens everywhere except one word that decides the meaning. No threshold separates P9 from N7, so no relaxation catches this without also inventing that one. It stays a miss, in the denominator.

scoring: real_disagreement says whether the two documents genuinely disagree. expect_detected says whether this scanner is expected to see it. Recall is measured against real_disagreement, so the 5 cases where the two differ count against the score: N5-qualified-exception, N6-incidental-negation, P6-retention-verb-outside-pattern-set, P8-adjective-drift, P9-attribute-noun-dropped. Three of those are real disagreements the scanner misses and two are false alarms it raises on documents that agree.
independence_caveat: Honest limits on how held-out this is. The first nine cases were written by the same author as the fix and, for the three paraphrase positives, follow the same 'The X for Y is N' against 'Y uses M X' shape as the planted pair with different nouns; the three original negatives are the three guards the implementation's own docstring names. That makes them a regression suite more than an independent sample. The six adversarial cases (N4 through N6, P7 through P9) were written by a reviewer working from the code with the opposite incentive, and four of the six still fail. N7, N8 and N9 came from a SECOND adversarial review and are the most valuable cases here, because they cover the shape the corpus had been missing altogether: two different subjects distinguished by a WORD rather than a numeral. Without them, a relaxation of topic matching measured as free. With them it measures as precision 0.5294, and it was reverted. One change has been made to the comparator in response to this corpus, unit-aware numeric comparison prompted by N4 and P7, and four stative verbs were added to the claim extractor; the rest of what this corpus prompted was measured and rejected.
